observer: George B. McClellan, dispatch to Halleck
evidence: Credits conspicuous management of the cavalry withdrawal from Harpers Ferry and recommends a major brevet.
limit: [I] Role-bounded execution appraisal. Recommendation is not proof that the brevet was granted, nor army-level competence or battlefield nerve.

evidence: Specifically credits gallant bridge defense and a vigorous flank charge at Sharpsburg.
limit: [I] Interested superior praising a subordinate after battle; bounded personal leadership, not verified enemy strength, a high centre, or an organising gift.

observer: Military commission, David Hunter president; finding promulgated in General Orders 183
evidence: Commission finds the Maryland Heights defense without ability, abandonment without sufficient cause and lack of military capacity; presidential dismissal follows.
limit: [I] Attributed official adverse assessment for this command, not an independent finding about every allegation or an innate low centre. Tyler had expected an explanation on 23 September; that expectation is retained as countervoice, not proof of acquittal. Observation/dismissal date is not the day the position was abandoned.
